message.content:
Build a BUSINESS EMAIL product (mailbox hosting per domain) for Nxeon at /opt/nxeon. Other agents edit OTHER areas concurrently — touch ONLY YOUR OWNED FILES.

## PRIMER
Next.js 15 + Prisma. `"use server"` = async-only. `import { db } from "@/lib/db"`; `import { requireUser, requireAdmin } from "@/lib/auth"`; admin RBAC `import { requireArea } from "@/lib/rbac"` → `requireArea("billing")`. Money = integer cents; charge via `import { debitWallet } from "@/lib/wallet"`. Design: `.card`,`.input`,`.btn-*`,`.table-shell`; `import { PageHeader, Badge, fmtMoney } from "@/components/ui/primitives"`. NEW models: `EmailPlan{ name, mailboxes, storageGB, priceCents, termMonths, active, sortOrder }`, `EmailSubscription{ userId, domainName, emailPlanId, emailPlan, status, autoRenew, expiresAt, mailboxes }`, `Mailbox{ subscriptionId, address, passwordEnc }`. The user's registered domains: `db.domain.findMany({ where:{ userId } })`.

## TASK (product + ordering SCAFFOLD — actual mail delivery is a pluggable provider integration; make that clear in the UI, don't fake sending)
1. **Admin plans** `/admin/email-plans` (`requireArea("billing")`): CRUD `EmailPlan` tiers (name, mailboxes, storage, price, term). `components/admin/EmailPlanControls.tsx`. `prisma/seed-email-plans.ts` seeds ~3 tiers (e.g. Starter 1 mailbox 10GB, Business 5/25GB, Pro 25/50GB); RUN it (`npx tsx prisma/seed-email-plans.ts`).
2. **Customer** `/dashboard/email` (`requireUser`): choose one of your domains + a plan → `orderEmailHosting(domainName, emailPlanId)` (debit wallet, create `EmailSubscription` ACTIVE + expiresAt). Then manage mailboxes: add/remove `Mailbox` rows (address@domain), shown with status. Include a clear "DNS setup required" panel that tells the user the MX/SPF records to add and links to their domain's DNS page (`/dashboard/domains`), plus a note that mailbox provisioning connects to the mail provider (integration pending — mark new subscriptions as provisioning).
3. `components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx` — the plan picker + mailbox manager.
`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts` (`"use server"`): `orderEmailHosting`, `addMailbox`, `removeMailbox`, `adminSaveEmailPlan`, `adminToggleEmailPlan`, `adminDeleteEmailPlan`.

## OWNED FILES (create ONLY these)
`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts`, `app/admin/email-plans/page.tsx`, `components/admin/EmailPlanControls.tsx`, `app/dashboard/email/page.tsx`, `components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx`, `prisma/seed-email-plans.ts`.

## HARD RULES
Never touch schema/next.config/layouts/Shell/lib(auth/db/rbac/mailer/actions*)/worker/app-other/ROADMAP/docs/sitemap or others' files (incl. any `domains/**` — another agent owns domain DNS). No build/prisma/generate/restart/commit. You MAY run the seed tsx. No new deps. `"use server"` = async-only. Ownership-check every op.

## REPORT
Files created; how ordering + mailbox mgmt work; confirm seed ran; INTEGRATION NEEDED (nav links `/dashboard/email`, `/admin/email-plans`; the mail-provider integration to actually create mailboxes; renewal billing for EmailSubscription); risks.

1	import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
2	import type { Role, User } from "@prisma/client";
3	import { realUser } from "./auth";
4	
5	/**
6	 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
7	 *
8	 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
9	 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
10	 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
11	 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
12	 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
13	 */
14	export type Area =
15	  | "overview"
16	  | "analytics"
17	  | "clients"
18	  | "support"
19	  | "fleet"
20	  | "billing"
21	  | "platform";
22	
23	/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
24	export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
25	  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
26	  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
27	  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
28	  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
29	  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
30	  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
31	  platform: ["ADMIN"],
32	};
33	
34	export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
35	  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
36	}
37	
38	/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
39	export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
40	  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
41	}
42	
43	/** Maps admin nav hrefs to their governing area. Unknown routes default to platform (ADMIN-only). */
44	const HREF_AREA: Record<string, Area> = {
45	  "/admin": "overview",
46	  "/admin/analytics": "analytics",
47	  "/admin/users": "clients",
48	  "/admin/support": "support",
49	  "/admin/servers": "fleet",
50	  "/admin/nodes": "fleet",
51	  "/admin/ips": "fleet",
52	  "/admin/provisioning": "fleet",
53	  "/admin/monitoring": "fleet",
54	  "/admin/infrastructure": "fleet",
55	  "/admin/subscriptions": "billing",
56	  "/admin/billing": "billing",
57	  "/admin/invoices": "billing",
58	  "/admin/plans": "billing",
59	  "/admin/coupons": "billing",
60	  "/admin/game-plans": "billing",
61	  "/admin/gift-codes": "billing",
62	  "/admin/feedback": "support",
63	  "/admin/orgs": "clients",
64	  "/admin/visitors": "analytics",

69	  "/admin/audit": "platform",

72	  "/admin/staff": "platform",
73	  "/admin/email-templates": "platform",
74	  "/admin/games": "platform",
75	  "/admin/blog": "platform",
76	};
77	
78	export function areaForHref(href: string): Area {
79	  return HREF_AREA[href] ?? "platform";
80	}
81	
82	export function canAccessHref(role: Role, href: string): boolean {
83	  return canAccess(role, areaForHref(href));
84	}
85	
86	/**
87	 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
88	 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
89	 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
90	 */
91	export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
92	  const user = await realUser();
93	  if (!user) redirect("/login");
94	  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
95	  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
96	  return user;
97	}

## Report

Built the Business Email (mailbox hosting per domain) product scaffold for Nxeon. All work confined to the six owned files.

### Files created
- `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-email-hosting.ts` — `"use server"` actions: `orderEmailHosting`, `addMailbox`, `removeMailbox`, `adminSaveEmailPlan`, `adminToggleEmailPlan`, `adminDeleteEmailPlan`.
- `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/email-plans/page.tsx` — admin catalogue page, gated by `requireArea("billing")`.
- `/opt/nxeon/components/admin/EmailPlanControls.tsx` — client CRUD controls (form/editor/toggle/delete).
- `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/email/page.tsx` — customer page, gated by `requireUser`.
- `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx` — plan picker + mailbox manager + DNS panel.
- `/opt/nxeon/prisma/seed-email-plans.ts` — seeds Starter/Business/Pro tiers.

### How it works
- **Admin plans**: CRUD over `EmailPlan` (name, mailboxes, storage GB/mailbox, price cents, term months, active, sortOrder). Delete is refused while subscriptions reference a tier (disable instead). All ops audit-logged.
- **Ordering**: customer selects one of their `ACTIVE` domains + an active plan → `orderEmailHosting` verifies domain ownership (`db.domain.findFirst({ name, userId })`), blocks duplicate subscriptions per domain, checks balance, then in one `$transaction` calls `debitWallet`, writes a `WalletTransaction`, and creates the `EmailSubscription` with `status: "ACTIVE"` and `expiresAt = addMonths(now, termMonths)`.
- **Mailbox management**: `addMailbox` enforces the plan's mailbox quota and address uniqueness, validates the local-part, and stores `address@domain` (no `passwordEnc` — no provider call). `removeMailbox` deletes after an ownership check via the parent subscription. Every op re-checks `subscription.userId === user.id`.
- **Provisioning honesty**: no mail is sent/faked. Subscriptions and every mailbox render a "Provisioning" badge with an explicit note that mailbox provisioning connects to a mail provider whose integration is pending. A "DNS setup required" panel shows example MX (`mx.nxeon.email`, prio 10) and SPF TXT records and links to `/dashboard/domains`.

### Design decision to flag
The schema's `EmailSubscription.status` comment enumerates `ACTIVE | SUSPENDED | CANCELLED`, so I kept the DB status `ACTIVE` (per task step 2) rather than inventing a `PROVISIONING` status value that other agents' admin subscription views might not expect. The "provisioning" state is surfaced entirely in the UI via badges + notes. Revisit if you'd prefer a real status value.

### Seed
Ran `npx tsx prisma/seed-email-plans.ts` — 3 tiers created (Starter 1mbx/10GB $1.99, Business 5/25GB $7.99, Pro 25/50GB $24.99). Idempotent (dedupes by name). Prisma client already had the email models generated.

### INTEGRATION NEEDED (not owned by me)
- **Nav links**: add `/dashboard/email` to the customer dashboard nav and `/admin/email-plans` to the admin nav (the admin route is already mapped to the `billing` area in `lib/rbac.ts` `HREF_AREA`, so RBAC works, but no nav link exists).
- **Mail-provider integration**: replace the placeholder DNS host values and actually create/delete mailboxes with the provider when `addMailbox`/`removeMailbox`/`orderEmailHosting` run (populate `Mailbox.passwordEnc`, real MX/SPF/DKIM records).
- **Renewal billing**: no worker/cron renews `EmailSubscription` at `expiresAt` (`autoRenew` is stored but unused) — the billing worker needs to charge and extend, mirroring VPS/domain renewals.

### Risks
- Type-check of all six owned files is clean; I did not run a full build/prisma/generate per the hard rules.
- Placeholder DNS values (`mx.nxeon.email`, `_spf.nxeon.email`) are illustrative and must be finalized by the provider integration.
- One subscription per domain is enforced in the action; there's no DB unique constraint (I can't touch schema), so a rare concurrent double-order could theoretically slip through — low risk given wallet debit + UI flow.
